headline: The hedge changed hands overnight — copper and a cracking dollar, not gold — while equity vol sits at the 9th percentile and bond vol keeps bidding.
summary: Yesterday's story was a one-day metals bid funded by a bond rally. Today only half of it survived. Gold is +0.7% to 4,197.8 but still -4.3% on the month, trend down, 17th percentile of its year, with GDX -7.6% and GDXJ -8.9% on the month. Copper is the one that held: +1.9% to 6.636, 91st percentile, and copper/gold +7.8% on the month (z=1.12, acc z=0.86) at the 94th percentile. That is a growth signal, not a fear signal. The dollar break is now three sessions old and broadening: DXY -0.3% to 101.66 (-0.5% on the week, though still +1.3% on the month at the 86th percentile), EURUSD +0.6% to 1.126, GBP +0.8%, USDKRW -0.6% and -2.4% on the month. Risk regime prints -11, with credit & vol at +22 and growth pulse +11 offsetting rates at -59.

What has not changed is the price of money, and that is the whole problem. The 30-year mortgage is 7.40%, +64bp on the month, z=1.91 with acceleration z=1.34, at the 100th percentile. The 3-month bill is 4.28%, also a 52-week high. The 10-year sits at 5.10% and 10-year real yields at 2.78% (+16bp on the month, 87th percentile) even after a 9bp rally. 2s10s is 33bp, -14bp on the week, 24th percentile. Against that, MOVE is 102.49, +22.4% on the month and +50.4% on three, while VIX is 16.14 at the 15th percentile and VIX3M 18.49 at the 9th, with SKEW at 160.45 in the 96th percentile. Equity vol is the cheapest thing on the tape and bond vol the dearest; somebody is wrong.

The disinflation impulse is now undeniable and the market still has not repriced the front end. WTI -2.2% to 95.85, -6.4% on the month with acceleration z=-1.76; RBOB -3.5% today, -6.9% on the week, -11.9% on the month; corn -10.8% (acc z=-2.24), wheat -9.5%, soybeans -4.6%. Five-year breakevens are 2.33% (-8bp on the month, 30th percentile), tens 2.32%. The inflation composite is -19. That makes the bill, not the long bond, the mispriced leg — and it leaves energy equities naked: XLE is at the 96th percentile and 17.0% above its 200-day while OIH is -8.5% on the month and rolling over.

Beneath the index, the damage is regional and specific. KOSPI is 5,668 — up 2.0% today but -14.5% on the week, -15.6% on the month, z=-2.27; EWY -11.5% on the month. The semis unwind is a week old and real: SMH -8.0%, SOXX -8.6%, MU -10.1%, AMD -9.4%, TSM -7.8% on the week, yet IGV/SMH is +8.7% over the same stretch — rotation inside tech, not exit. Breadth composite is -16: IWM/SPY sits at the 10.7th percentile (-5.6% on the month, z=-1.51), XHB/SPY the 6th, KRE/SPY the 22.6th. Credit still refuses to confirm: HYG -1.2% on the month, HYG/IEF -1.0% with z=-0.92. And the single most extreme print in the entire digest is USDMXN: +7.2% on the month, z=2.65, acceleration z=1.54, turning up — against USDBRL -1.3% and EWZ +10.1%. LatAm is splitting in two.

good.text: Dollar break confirmed and broadening: DXY -0.3% to 101.66 and -0.5% on the week, EURUSD +0.6% to 1.126, GBP +0.8%, USDKRW -0.6% (-2.4% 1m), CEW +0.5%. Global funding pressure is easing at the margin.

Copper +1.9% to 6.636 at the 91st percentile, and copper/gold +7.8% on the month (z=1.12, acc z=0.86, 94th percentile). The cyclical metal is leading the precious one — that is the right configuration for risk.

Real disinflation, not just base effects: RBOB -11.9% on the month, WTI -6.4% (acc z=-1.76), corn -10.8%, wheat -9.5%, and 5y breakevens at 2.33% in the 30th percentile. Consumer real income gets a tailwind and the Fed gets cover.

Crypto, the purest liquidity beta, is turning up from the floor: BTC +8.4% on the month at 82,511 (11.9% above its 200d), SOL +8.5%, IBIT +8.1%, MSTR +16.7% (+60.9% on three months) — all from sub-45th 52-week percentiles.

Health care is the cleanest leadership on the tape: XLV +6.1% on the month at the 100th percentile with relative strength turning up and acc z=1.08, LLY +10.2%, UNH +8.2%, IHI +5.7% on the week. Quality factor QUAL at the 98th percentile.
Defensive-consumer and retail cash flow improving: XRT +5.8% on the month with rs +3.5% and acc z=1.22, WMT +9.0% (z=1.25), COST +8.5%. Consistent with the gasoline collapse feeding through.

bad.text: The rates composite is -59 and the cost of capital is still accelerating: 30y mortgage 7.40% (+64bp 1m, z=1.91, acc z=1.34, 100th percentile), 3m bill 4.28% at a 52-week high, 10y real yield 2.78%. Homebuilders bounced 3-4% into a tightening they cannot absorb.

Volatility is mispriced across asset classes in opposite directions: MOVE 102.49 (+22.4% 1m, +50.4% 3m) versus VIX 16.14 at the 15th percentile and VIX3M at the 9th, with SKEW 160.45 in the 96th. Tail demand is high, front vol is free.

Breadth is still broken under the one-day pops: IWM/SPY 10.7th percentile (-5.6% 1m, z=-1.51), RSP/SPY -1.3% on the month and trend down, XHB/SPY 6th percentile, IYT/SPY 17.8th. The breadth & appetite composite is -16.

Korea is still unwinding: KOSPI -14.5% on the week and -15.6% on the month with z=-2.27, EWY -11.5%, and the AI hardware chain bleeding with it — SMH -8.0%, SOXX -8.6%, MU -10.1%, AMD -9.4%, TSM -7.8% over five sessions.

The peso is the biggest dislocation in the digest: USDMXN +7.2% on the month, z=2.65, acceleration z=1.54, turning up — a carry unwind running while EEM/SPY is -4.8% on the month (z=-1.14) and rolling over.

Credit refuses to ratify the equity bounce: HYG -1.2% on the month and rolling over, HYG/IEF -1.0% with z=-0.92, BKLN z=-0.68, and the financial complex leading lower — KBE -5.9% 1m, GS -8.7%, BX -13.8%.

trades.name: Copper over gold
trades.line: Long FCX vs short GLD - copper/gold at 94th pctile
trades.expr: Equal-dollar long FCX (or Dec HG copper futures) against short GLD. Scale 1:1 notional; FCX is the higher-beta leg, so half-size it if running the futures version.
trades.thesis: The portfolio hedge is rotating from the fear metal to the growth metal. Copper is backed by a falling dollar and a 33.8% year-over-year price; gold has lost its real-yield sponsor with 10y TIPS at 2.78% and no crisis bid showing up in credit.
trades.trigger: Copper +1.9% today to 6.636 (91st percentile) while gold's two-day bounce leaves it -4.3% on the month, trend down, 17th percentile. Copper/gold +7.8% on the month, z=1.12, acc z=0.86, 94th percentile and 15.4% above its 200-day. Gold miners gave the move back: GDX -7.6%, GDXJ -8.9% on the month.
trades.stop: Gold closing above 4,400 on a renewed real-yield collapse, or copper losing 6.30.
trades.target: Copper 7.20; another 10% on the copper/gold ratio.

trades.name: Short energy equities
trades.line: Short XLE: crude -6.4% 1m, sector still at 96th pctile
trades.expr: Short XLE outright, or beta-matched against long SPY. Higher-beta version: short XOP. Avoid shorting the barrel itself — Brent is still +20.5% on three months.
trades.thesis: Energy equities are priced for permanent triple-digit Brent while the barrel, the crack and the service complex all roll over simultaneously. XLE is 17.0% above its 200-day at the 96th percentile with month relative strength already negative.
trades.trigger: WTI -2.2% today to 95.85, -6.4% on the month with acceleration z=-1.76. RBOB -3.5% today, -6.9% on the week, -11.9% on the month. OIH -8.5% on the month, rolling over, rs -10.4%. XOP rs -4.1% on the month despite +17.6% on three.
trades.stop: Brent closes above 112 (it is 106.19) or WTI reclaims 100 with gasoline turning back up.
trades.target: XLE down 10% toward 60, i.e. back to its 200-day.

trades.name: Brazil over Mexico
trades.line: Long EWZ / short EWW - BRL firm, peso z=2.65 blowout
trades.expr: Equal-dollar long EWZ against short EWW. Cleaner institutional version: long BVSP futures hedged, short MXN spot against USD.
trades.thesis: LatAm is splitting. Brazil has both currency and index momentum; Mexico's local index gains are being eaten alive by the currency, so the dollar-based ETF goes nowhere while the peso carry trade unwinds.
trades.trigger: USDMXN +7.2% on the month with z=2.65 and acceleration z=1.54 — the largest z-score in the entire digest — versus USDBRL -1.3% on the month. EWZ +10.1% on the month with rs +7.7% and BVSP z=1.58; EWW -0.2% on the month despite MXX +6.5%, with EWW rs -2.3%.
trades.stop: USDMXN back under 17.80, or EWZ losing its 200-day (13.3% below spot).

trades.name: 2s30s bull steepener
trades.line: Long front end vs short long bond: bills are the mispriced leg
trades.expr: Long 2-year futures (TU) against duration-weighted short 30-year (UB). Cash proxy: long SHY versus short TLT, duration-matched.
trades.thesis: The commodity and breakeven complex has already repriced disinflation; the bill has not. Meanwhile the 30-year carries the term premium and the deficit, so the rally should come from the front, not the back.
trades.trigger: 3m bill 4.28% at the 100th percentile while 5y breakevens are 2.33% at the 30th percentile and RBOB is -11.9% on the month. 2y and 5y acceleration z-scores are -1.11 and -1.04 — yields are already decelerating at the front. 2s10s flattened to 33bp, -14bp on the week, 24th percentile. A 7.40% mortgage with acc z=1.34 is doing the tightening the front end has not priced.

trades.name: Own cheap equity tail
trades.line: Buy SPX put spread: VIX3M 9th pctile vs MOVE +50% 3m
trades.expr: Buy a 2-month SPX ~5% OTM put spread (7,400/6,900 area) for 50-75bp of NAV. Alternative: VIX Dec 20/30 call spread. Do not sell upside against it — SKEW says calls are not where the risk is.
trades.thesis: The two vol markets disagree violently. Rates vol is pricing a regime change, equity vol is pricing none. With credit not confirming the equity bounce, convexity is the cheapest hedge available.
trades.trigger: VIX 16.14 at the 15th percentile, VIX3M 18.49 at the 9th, term structure 0.89 — while MOVE is 102.49, +22.4% on the month and +50.4% on three. SKEW 160.45 at the 96th percentile. HYG/IEF z=-0.92 and the breadth composite at -16.
trades.stop: Defined by premium. Monetize if VIX3M trades above 24; let it expire if SPX holds above 7,900.

trades.name: Crypto beta on the dollar break
trades.line: Long IBIT with a COIN kicker - BTC +8.4% 1m, trend turning up
trades.expr: Long IBIT as the core, 2:1 against a smaller COIN position for torque. Size to 1-1.5% of NAV given realized vol.
trades.thesis: The highest-beta liquidity gauge turned before anything else and is doing so against a falling dollar from deeply washed-out percentiles — the classic setup for a multi-week catch-up rather than a dead-cat bounce.
trades.trigger: BTC 82,511, +8.4% on the month and 11.9% above its 200-day, trend state turning up from the 43rd percentile. IBIT +8.1%, SOL +8.5%, MSTR +16.7% on the month (+60.9% on three), COIN +6.3% in a session from the 19th percentile. ETH/BTC turning up. DXY -0.5% on the week.
trades.stop: BTC closing below 74,000 (its 200-day) kills the trade.

trades.name: Health care over financials
trades.line: Long XLV / short XLF - 100th pctile vs a 33bp curve
trades.expr: Equal-dollar long XLV against short XLF. Concentrated version: long LLY and UNH versus short KRE.
trades.thesis: One sector has leadership and accelerating relative strength; the other needs a steeper curve and better credit, and is getting neither. Banks cannot earn into 2s10s at 33bp with loan and HY spreads quietly widening.
trades.trigger: XLV +6.1% on the month at the 100th percentile, rs +3.9% and turning up, acc z=1.08; LLY +10.2% on the month, UNH +8.2%. XLF -2.4% on the month with rs -4.5% and rolling over; KBE -5.9%, KRE -5.3%, GS -8.7%, BX -13.8%. 2s10s 33bp, 24th percentile, flattening 14bp on the week.
trades.stop: KRE/SPY reclaiming its 200-day (about 7% above spot) alongside HYG/IEF turning up, or XLV relative strength rolling over.
